 Stocks plunge as midterm results send AI trade into a tailspin
 By Elisabeth Buchwald , John Towfighi , Matt Egan 
 Updated Nov 5, 2026, 11:12 AM ET 
 PUBLISHED Nov 5, 2026, 10:47 AM ET 
 Pedestrians outside the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York, on Friday, October 16. The Nasdaq was on pace Thursday for its worst day since April 2025, when President Donald Trump unveiled sweeping global tariffs. 
 Michael Nagle/Bloomberg/Getty Images

 The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite plunged by as much as 5.5% Thursday as investors weighed whether Democrats’ gains in the midterm elections could lead to a slowdown in the massive data center buildout.
 The Nasdaq dipped into correction territory, trading down more than 10% from its record high on October 6 and on pace for the worst day in five months. It’s a sharp reversal after Wednesday’s historic post-midterm rally with the Nasdaq gaining 1.44%.
 While the Nasdaq rose Wednesday, underneath the surface, shares of semiconductor chipmakers and companies involved in the AI data center buildout were falling. That selling pressure intensified on Thursday, dragging the index down sharply.
 Related article
 In an aerial view, sections of the Stargate Oracle AI data center undergoes construction on August 26, 2026 in Abilene, Texas. 
 Brandon Bell/Getty Images 
 America got the anti-data-center wave it voted for. Here come the economic consequences 
 6 min read 
 Shares of chipmakers and the “picks and shovels” of the data center buildout and AI boom are selling off as investors mull the implications of Democrats winning races in states like Texas that are hubs for planned data centers.
 The Nasdaq has been on a rollercoaster this year: The tech-heavy index closed in correction in March , rallied back to record highs in early June, stumbled and nearly fell into correction in late July, then reclaimed record highs in September and October — before sliding into correction territory again on Thursday.
 This is a developing story and will be updated.
